tree.name: Family tree in silhouettes

data.note: Four generations, most of Scotland's lights

people.name: Thomas Smith
people.story: The Northern Lighthouse Board's first engineer, a lamp-maker by trade. He married Robert's mother; later Robert married his daughter.

people.name: Robert Stevenson
people.works: Bell Rock, Isle of May, Sumburgh Head, Cape Wrath, Mull of Galloway
people.story: Engineer of the Bell Rock, he spent his life building lights on Scotland's headlands, and devised the flashing light.

people.name: Alan Stevenson
people.story: The eldest son, builder of Skerryvore. A master of lenses, he brought Fresnel's lens to Britain's lighthouses.

people.name: David Stevenson
people.works: Muckle Flugga, Butt of Lewis, Dubh Artach
people.story: With his brother Thomas he took on the family firm, and lit Muckle Flugga at Britain's northern tip.

people.name: Thomas Stevenson
people.works: Muckle Flugga, Dubh Artach, the Stevenson screen
people.story: He improved lighthouse lenses and reflectors, and invented the slatted box that holds every weather station's thermometers.

people.name: David Alan Stevenson
people.story: David's son, who carried on building; the Flannan Isles light was his.

people.name: Charles Stevenson
people.story: David's other son, who worked beside his brother on the lights.

people.name: D. Alan Stevenson
people.story: Charles's son, the last lighthouse engineer of the family, who also wrote a history of the world's lighthouses.

people.name: Robert Louis Stevenson
people.story: Thomas's son. He trained as a lighthouse engineer and went out to the works with his father — then became a writer, of Treasure Island and Jekyll and Hyde. The family's most famous son built no lighthouse at all.

brief.subject: The Stevenson family
brief.intent: Most of Scotland's lighthouses came from four generations of one family; and its most famous son went off to write novels
brief.audience: Anyone who likes history and lives
brief.concept: A family tree growing to the right: each person a silhouette ringed in the colour of their lights on the map, with what they left under their name; picking someone tells their story and lights their line back. Last of all, Louis — who wrote Treasure Island.
brief.direction: Victorian silhouette portraits, warm white paper and fine lines, a colour for each builder
